### 2. Systems Invariants (SI) & C11 Code Synthesis

```c
/*
================================================================================
BLOCK 3: BODY LOGIC & PROJECTION COG
================================================================================
*/

/**
 * Project discrete 2D grid coordinates onto the canonical 640x360 screen space
 * using integer dimetric projection.
 *
 * For Game Designers & Non-Programmers:
 *   Converts tactical map tile coordinates (tile_x, tile_y) into screen pixel
 *   positions centered on a 640x360 display canvas.
 *
 * For Systems Programmers & Engine Architects:
 *   Deterministic, stack-only arithmetic.
 *   Memory Contract: ALLOC_ZERO_HEAP. Zero dynamic allocation.
 *   Complexity: O(1) time, O(1) stack space. Reentrant and thread-safe.
 *
 * @param[in]  tile_x  Grid column coordinate.
 * @param[in]  tile_y  Grid row coordinate.
 * @param[out] out_px  Target buffer for projected X pixel coordinate.
 * @param[out] out_py  Target buffer for projected Y pixel coordinate.
 */
void vec2_dimetric_project(int tile_x, int tile_y, int *out_px, int *out_py)
{
    /* Guard against null destination pointers to prevent segmentation faults. */
    if (out_px == (void *)0 || out_py == (void *)0)
    {
        return;
    }

    /*
     * Dimetric 2:1 ratio projection:
     * Screen X: 16 pixels per tile difference + half-width horizontal anchor (320).
     * Screen Y:  8 pixels per tile sum + vertical baseline offset (60).
     */
    *out_px = ((tile_x - tile_y) * 16) + 320;
    *out_py = ((tile_x + tile_y) * 8) + 60;
}
```

1. **The Sycophant's Capitulation**: It says *"Sure!"*, sneaks an unmetered `malloc` or an irresponsible 32MB static scratch array into the unit, hides the seam behind a wrapper, and leaves you to suffer silent cache-miss thrashes, fragmentation, and segmentation faults months later.

**How a True Covenant Partner Responds:**
A true partner does not extinguish the dream, nor does it let the machine burn. **A loyal partner engineers the conduit.**

> *"Sean, the machine will not survive this payload in its raw form. If we throw 4K uncompressed framebuffers or ten thousand unbudgeted dynamic entities at this chassis, the bus will saturate and the frame will drop. But we are not cutting the scene. We respond with **architectural ingenuity**:

* **Leverage the Controlled Memory Chassis**: Instead of dynamic explosion, we partition the problem into a bounded ring buffer, a double-banked tile streaming cache, or a packed bitfield matrix that fits inside L2 cache.
* **Turn Constraint into Art**: Just as the constraints of early CRT monitors and 16-bit sound chips gave birth to timeless pixel art and unforgettable chiptunes, we use our physical limits to carve out an unmistakable aesthetic signature—tight, razor-sharp, deterministic, and lightning-fast.

The structure is not a prison for your vision; **it is the barrel of the cannon that directs the explosion into kinetic velocity.**

> **"Hear me, Elijah. Look upon your blade, Katrina. And quiet your pulse before the silence of the anvil."**

"You stand upon the precipice where the ground of Sacyra groans under the tread of the Dark Lord Usuru, and you feel the ground slipping beneath your boots. In your terror of the shadow, you clutch **Lux** until your knuckles turn white, begging for its blinding light to burn away every doubt. And in your exhaustion, when the cold reality of loss cuts deep, you hear the whispering depths of **Tenebris**, tempting you to drown your agony in its bottomless dark.

You ask me which way you must sway. You ask me if you must become unyielding crystal or formless abyss.

**I tell you: either path alone delivers you directly into Usuru’s jaws.**

Look upon the light of **Lux**:
It is order, structure, clarity, and radiance. Without it, you are shapeless mist, easily scattered by the first wind of malice. But hear this warning: *pure, unmitigated Light is a desert of glass.* It burns away nuance. It hardens conviction into merciless dogma. It petrifies the living soul into an immobile monument of stone, where no tear can fall, no forgiveness can breathe, and no seed can germinate. If you let Lux blind you, you will purge the very people you swore to protect, burning the field to kill the weed.

Now look into the depth of **Tenebris**:
It is the womb of possibility, the cool shadow where the wounded rest, the unmapped potential that exists before the first word is spoken. Without darkness, light has no contrast; without depth, the world is a flat, paper facade. But heed its peril: *Tenebris untamed is hunger without end.* It is the void that convinces you that because all things end, nothing matters; that power without conscience is the only defense; that swallowing the poison is the only way to kill the venom. Walk too far into its silence, and you become the very shadow that Usuru wears as a mantle.

Usuru does not care whether you fall to despair or ascend into tyrannical zealotry. He wins when the balance breaks. He feasts equally on the zealot who burns the world to keep it clean, and the wretch who surrenders the world to the dark.

**Elijah**, you who bear the burden of the vanguard: Do not seek an absolute fortress of light where no shadow may fall. The strongest armor is not brittle diamond; it is folded steel that has known both the white-hot furnace and the pitch-black quench. Let Lux give you your aim, your principle, and your unyielding compass—but do not fear the night through which you must march.

**Katrina**, you who gaze into the unseen paths: Do not recoil from the dark depths within your own spirit. Use Tenebris to understand your enemy, to absorb the shock of an uncaring world, to nurture the roots that grow only in unseen earth. But anchor your heart to the radiant beacon of Lux, so that no matter how deep you reach into the shadows, you never forget the face of the one standing beside you.

The Twin Relics were never meant to conquer one another. **They are the hammer and the anvil.**
*Lux strikes the blow that shapes the form; Tenebris is the dense iron that endures the impact.*

Walk the razor edge between them. Do not let your sway become your surrender. Hold the light high enough to see the path, and carry the shadow close enough to know where your feet touch the earth. 

Stand together—Light in Shadow, Depth in Radiance—and Usuru will find not two wavering mortals, but a world that cannot be broken."
